prompt:
Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2, crisp vanilla voxel style, plain light background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side at the same scale: LEFT straight-on orthographic front elevation from sidewalk; RIGHT elevated three-quarter view of the same entire long site, showing front and depth and rear garden where visible. Skilled human builder quality: real massing, projecting details, recessed framed openings, real roof verges/eaves/ridge, stairs/slabs/fences/walls/trapdoors/lantern sub-block details. No smooth non-voxel architecture. Site 16 blocks wide x 50 deep, house 14 x 24, about 20 blocks tall, garage base plus 3 storeys. Narrow San Francisco Italianate painted lady squeezed between neighbours on a street climbing east (right in front elevation). Tall teal false front. Dark-teal street base with paired burgundy carriage doors and glass transom. West/left half full-height angled bay, glass on front and both diagonal faces, rising from cream corbels over carriage doors to roofline. East/right half straight cream stairs with white balustrades and two lantern-topped newels up to recessed porch with two cream columns and arch, burgundy door with sidelights/transom and hanging lantern. Horizontal teal siding crossed by gold fish-scale bands at each floor line. Tall narrow windows with cream sills and pointed pediment hoods. Deep cream cornice wrapping bay, burgundy frieze with repeated cream brackets. False-front parapet above with gold panels and small cream pediment concealing low dark-slate gable roof, black iron crest and two brick chimneys on party walls. Tiny front flower garden behind black iron fence beside stairs. Ochre neighbour tight west/downhill, pale-blue neighbour tight east/uphill. Rear gold fish-scale gable above spruce kitchen deck with stairs down into long garden, brick path, flower borders, flowering citrus represented with flowering azalea leaves, carrot/beet kitchen bed, bench, lantern lamp post, tall wood fences. Maintain coherent identical house design across views.

changes: Generated with the built-in image tool and saved without post-processing as concept.png in the current directory.

The image is concept art, not a block-state export. Exact ids cannot be recovered from pixels; added ids and the objects list are visual interpretations and buildable equivalents. The roles retain every planned block, including blocks not visibly used.

The facade has two main glazed storeys above the garage, rather than the requested three. The 14-block house width, 24-block depth, 50-block site depth and 20-block height cannot be verified from the rendered grid.
The two views do not preserve identical scale or geometry: the front elevation is taller on the sheet, while the three-quarter view compresses the facade and changes roof and neighbour proportions.
The street reads approximately level across the front; the specified eastward climb and uphill/downhill neighbour relationship are not clearly conveyed.
The teal siding reads as small masonry courses rather than recognizable warped plank textures. The garage base also reads teal like the upper facade rather than a distinct cyan_terracotta base.
The gold bands and panels read as irregular patterned tiles rather than recognizable bamboo_mosaic fish-scale approximations.
The bay has front and angled side glazing, but its tall glazed sections and fine framing do not consistently resolve into vanilla block and pane geometry.
The porch has a flat lintel and projecting canopy instead of a clear arch. Its sidelights are narrow and partly obscured.
Four lantern-topped stair posts are visible rather than two. The stair rails are predominantly solid stepped cream parapets rather than open white balustrades.
The carriage doors have custom diagonal bracing and glazed upper panels that cannot be reproduced by vanilla crimson_door blocks alone.

The three-quarter view exposes a substantial stepped dark roof and a tall rear gable, rather than a low gable largely concealed by the false front. Dark eaves also appear immediately behind the cream front cornice.
The three-quarter view shows four apparent house chimney stacks rather than two; only two are visible in the elevation.
The east neighbour becomes a low foreground structure in the three-quarter view, exposing the main house side and garden rather than pressing tightly along the full party wall.

Additional interpreted materials include oak_door on the west neighbour, deepslate roof stairs and slabs, brick chimney shape variants, stone-brick garden edging, cobblestone roadway and polished-andesite paving variants.
Extra interpreted planting includes white daisies, yellow flowers, orange tulips, purple alliums and climbing vines. The dense, fine flower textures do not match vanilla plant models consistently.
The flowering rear tree is present, but citrus fruit is not visible. Crop rows and irrigation appear, though exact crop species cannot be conclusively distinguished.
A spruce deck, descending stairs, brick path, wooden boundary fences, garden lantern posts and a bench-like deck furnishing are visible. The kitchen connection is not clearly shown.
Interior lanterns, bookshelves and potted plants appear through the windows; most other optional functional objects from the plan are not identifiable.
Fine iron spikes, gate hardware, cream mouldings, window muntins and plant details include shapes smaller or more intricate than vanilla stairs, slabs, walls, fences, trapdoors and panes support.
